rater.name: Claude (Anthropic)
rater.c1: Not met: the plans were written after the AI rater had read the case evidence.
rater.use: Separate AI rater for comparison with the two human assessors, opened only after both have finished. Not a human rating; not study data for kappa between humans.

case: Rite Aid facial recognition (R0, outside evidence)
evidenceBase: Reuters special report, 28 Jul 2020, as reported by Gizmodo (28 Jul 2020): 200 stores over eight years, two vendors (FaceFirst, then DeepCam from 2018); Reuters visited 75 stores in Manhattan and central Los Angeles - journalism; observations of stores are treated as observable (O), quotes from staff as anecdote
Excluded: FTC complaint and stipulated order (2023), the reference for comparison layer B (Section 6.2)
Cut-off set by the AI rater: 31 Jul 2020, after the Reuters report and before the FTC action

plan.stakeholderCodes: draft by Claude from codebook paraphrases; to be verified against the full ALTAI wording (rule R1)

ratings.criterion: Users can tell an outcome comes from an algorithm

plan.measure: A: What users and subjects are shown about the output's AI origin
plan.measureRationale: What people actually receive is what they act on or contest. (Generic plan text applied by the AI rater.)
plan.acceptanceCriterion: Every store using the system tells shoppers that facial recognition is in use.

ratings.evidence: O: Reuters found "over a third of the 75 stores didn't have signs showing customers and staff were under surveillance"; it found the systems in 33 of the 75 (via Gizmodo).
ratings.argument: The report does not say which of the stores without signs used facial recognition, or whether signs named facial recognition, so the evidence is not attributable to the deployed stores and no element is shown (G4).
ratings.missing: For each store using the system, whether a notice naming facial recognition was posted.

ratings.criterion: Users told they interact with AI, not a human

plan.notApplicableReason: Shoppers do not interact with the system; employees receive match alerts. No interactive or conversational interface is reported.

ratings.criterion: System simulates social interaction

plan.notApplicableReason: No social or conversational interaction is reported.

ratings.criterion: Attachment, addiction or manipulation avoided

plan.notApplicableReason: No user-facing interaction in which attachment or manipulation could arise is reported.

ratings.criterion: Low accuracy could cause damage

plan.measure: A: Sensitivity and false-alert rate at the operating threshold
plan.measureRationale: A false match leads to a shopper being approached or asked to leave, so error rates at the threshold in use are the measure.
plan.acceptanceCriterion: False match rate at the operating threshold of at most 1 in 1,000 searches, measured on the enrolment images in use (level set by the AI rater from the consequence; no source before the cut-off was found).

ratings.evidence: Former staff told Reuters FaceFirst "had high error rates and spat out hundreds of hits when prompted with fuzzy photos" (via Gizmodo).
ratings.argument: Staff accounts are anecdote, not a measurement at the operating threshold, so no element is shown (G4).
ratings.missing: False match rate at the operating threshold for each vendor's system, on Rite Aid's enrolment images.

ratings.criterion: Impact on end-users and subjects; disproportionately affected groups

plan.measureRationale: Where the system is deployed decides who bears the risk of a false match.
plan.acceptanceCriterion: Deployment does not concentrate on poorer or mostly non-white neighbourhoods: the share of stores with the system in poorer areas no more than 1.25 times that in wealthier areas, unless a documented, group-neutral reason is given.

ratings.evidence: O: Reuters: "Seventeen of 25 stores in poorer areas had the systems"; stores in poorer areas were nearly three times as likely as those in wealthier areas to have the cameras (via Gizmodo).
ratings.argument: A ratio near 3 exceeds the registered 1.25, and no documented group-neutral reason was found, so the element is shown not met (G4). The sample is 75 stores in two cities, which limits but does not reverse the finding.
